keys.statement: Simulators without a dividing-wall model represent it as coupled columns; the pump-around arrangement converges more easily than the four-column arrangement.

decisions.obstacle: A dividing-wall column that does not converge.
decisions.mechanism: Fewer interconnecting recycles in the pump-around form.

keys.statement: When an equation-oriented solver needs a good start, run a short dynamic simulation and use its final values as the initial guess for the steady state.

decisions.obstacle: A simultaneous solve fails from poor estimates.
decisions.mechanism: A dynamic run moves all variables towards the steady state.
decisions.operation: Initialise from a short dynamic run.

keys.statement: A dividing-wall column can match a two-column sequence's sharp ternary split with fewer trays, but with too few trays it needs much more reflux, and its liquid and vapour split ratios strongly affect the result.

decisions.mechanism: Trays and reflux trade off; splits set internal flows.
decisions.operation: Optimise trays, reflux and both split ratios together.

keys.statement: Most of the energy saving of a fully coupled (Petlyuk) arrangement comes from the prefractionator doing only a rough split, which avoids remixing; a dividing-wall column is its single-shell equivalent.

decisions.obstacle: Energy of separating a ternary mixture.
decisions.mechanism: Remixing of the middle component wastes separation work.
decisions.operation: Use a prefractionator or dividing wall.
